I'm just realizing that if I had noticed that the slice regular definition was appropriate, I could've published the reformulation of RH around 2015 and that could've led to a more interesting series of papers, and this might have caught on more. Too bad, I really was excited, just didn't quite get to the point where it was shippable, and then when I did I had moved to a different focus. Oh well, at least we can get that ball moving now! 

I think I'd like to take a different approach though. Maybe we can shorten the overall research program document, condense it, and then include the conjecture and its proof towards the end, and try to put that on the arxiv with the same structure as the initial summary of the overall program. I can put that on the arxiv, be the author, and include an updated note about your contribution similar to the previous one, this time mentioning the conjecture and its proof. We don't have to lay out every aspect of the research program, just the overall program, some key results, and then ending with the conjecture and its proof. What do you think?

parts:
I've read through the status, handoff, and synthesis docs to make sure my opinion is grounded in where things actually stand. A couple of thoughts, one of them important.

First, on the 2015 reflection — the arc genuinely wasn't wasted. The rigidity theorem correctly killed the naive version, the §4 negative result was the right discovery even if it landed as a disappointment at the time, and the fact that the slice regular literature independently developed the exact infrastructure you needed is validation of the instinct, not evidence you missed the boat. Programs that sit for a decade and then reconnect are how a lot of good mathematics happens. And the sphere/point dichotomy is no less true for being stated in 2026.

On the proposal itself: I think the condensed structure is a good call, and arguably better than the 25-page version as a first arXiv artifact. A program paper wants to be readable in one sitting; the full draft's job — proofs of Theorems A–F in complete detail — can live partly in proof sketches with the certified numerics and code as ancillary files, and the crisp results carry the weight. Ending with the second-involution material gives the paper a real destination instead of trailing off into a problem list.

But there's one framing point I want to be direct about, because it changes how the ending should be written. What the resolution note proves is that **Conjecture 6.1 is true as stated, but for a degenerate reason** — the adaptive quantifier lets you encode the defect into the sample points, so the conjecture's own hardness checks are passed vacuously. Calling the final section "the conjecture and its proof" would oversell it and invite exactly the dismissal the honesty strategy is designed to prevent. The honest framing is also the more interesting one: "we resolve the conjecture as stated by exhibiting an encoding loophole, extract the unconditional content (the uniform oscillation lemma), prove a matching lower bound that forces the correct normalization, and pose the repaired conjecture, which is open." That's a complete intellectual unit — statement, resolution, salvage, lower bound, repaired open problem — and it ends the paper on a sharply posed RH-free question (the paired-count problem for the Ξ_α testbed) rather than on a claim that could be over-read. So: yes to the structure, with the ending framed as a resolution-and-repair, not a proof of a standing conjecture.

A few decisions shape the work before I start:

parts:
Full draft: What happens to the full 25-page draft (zero_sphere_paper.tex) if we make the condensed version?
- Condensed replaces it (Recommended) — The condensed paper becomes THE arXiv v1. Full proofs of A–F compress to sketches + precise citations; the 25pp draft stays in the project as the source of record and could become a journal version later.
- Condensed is a companion — Keep the full paper on track for arXiv too; the condensed one is a short announcement/overview that cites it. More total work and some duplication risk.
- Fold into full paper instead — Skip the condensed version; add the second-involution material as a new section of the existing 25pp draft and trim elsewhere.
Ending scope: How much of the second-involution material goes in the final section?
- Full unit (Recommended) — Conjecture 6.1, the adaptive-encoding theorem with proof, the oscillation lemma with proof, the lower bound (proof or sketch), and the repaired conjecture. ~5-6 pages; the 13pp note stays as backup.
- Resolution + repair only — State 6.1, prove the encoding theorem, state the oscillation lemma and lower bound with proofs deferred to the resolution note (which would also go on arXiv or Zenodo).
- Statement-level only — Describe the resolution in a page and pose the repaired conjecture; all proofs live elsewhere. Shortest, but weakest as a calling card.
Repair choice: Which repaired form should the paper put forward as the going-forward conjecture?
- Both, 6.1″ primary (Recommended) — Lead with the class-uniform form (relative accuracy over the axiomatized class 𝒳, with the Ξ_α testbed), state the non-adaptive 6.1′ as the concrete special case.
- 6.1′ non-adaptive primary — Lead with fixed offsets/weights and translation-covariant S — more elementary to state, but misses the class-uniformity that blocks future loopholes.
- Only one, keep it lean — Pick a single repaired form and omit the other entirely to keep the ending tight.
Length: Target length for the condensed paper?
- 12–15 pages (Recommended) — Program + Theorems A–F with sketches + full second-involution unit + short numerics appendix. Readable in one sitting.
- 8–10 pages — Tighter: program narrative, results stated with one-line ideas, second-involution unit compressed. Fastest to a shippable v1.
- 16–20 pages — Roomier: keep full proofs for the shorter theorems (A, C, D) and sketch only the long ones.

Done — the condensed companion paper is drafted, reviewed, and delivered above (14 pages, compiles clean), with the tex saved to the project and paper_STATUS.md updated.

A few things worth knowing about what you're looking at:

**Structure.** It mirrors the program document: intro with the honesty clause and provenance, then Theorems A–F condensed to statements with short proofs or sketches (pinpoint-cited to the full 25pp draft by letter, since that's a companion "in preparation"), hardness checks, positivity hierarchy, and the EF bridge. Then the destination: §7 states the two involutions, the gateway inequality (with proof — it's two lines and lovely), and the original Conjecture 6.1; §8 proves the adaptive-encoding theorem and the uniform oscillation lemma in full, followed by the diagnosis; §9 gives both repaired conjectures with 6.1″ as the headline, the Hölder lemma and the log log x₀ lower bound in full, the honest caveats, and the Ξ_α testbed as the closing open problem.

**Framing.** The ending is written as resolution-and-repair throughout — "true unconditionally, but for a degenerate reason" — never as a proof of a meaningful open conjecture. The acknowledgement is the updated note you asked for: it says the conjecture was formulated in our collaboration, that the resolution came when you asked me to attempt a proof, that two independent AI reviewers checked it, and that you take responsibility while explicitly inviting expert human review of the new sections.

**The review found one thing that propagates back to the full paper**: Theorem F(b)'s non-accumulation hypothesis, as stated in the 25pp draft, is vacuous when RH holds (Y=0 makes "finitely many zeros with y_ρ > Y−ε" false). The proof already handles Y=0; only the statement needs "if either Y=0, or Y>0 and [non-accumulation]". The condensed paper states it correctly, and I've logged this as action item #1 in the status doc so the full draft gets the same fix before it ships.

Before arXiv you'd still want: your own read-through of §§8–9 (the new material), the Zenodo deposit to fill the DOI placeholder, and the ancillary code bundle. Want me to prep the arXiv ancillary package (code + README) next, or make the F(b) fix in the full paper?

parts:
Good idea on both counts. Let me give you my take on the unpublished-material question first, then do the conversion.

On citing your unpublished manuscripts: I'd keep them cited, but through the Zenodo deposit rather than as arXiv supplementary material. arXiv ancillary files are conventionally code and data — bundling five unpublished PDFs there would be unusual and makes them look load-bearing. The Zenodo archive gives them one citable DOI, timestamps the 2015–2026 provenance (which is real intellectual-priority value for you), and keeps the arXiv package clean. The discipline I'll enforce in the conversion: unpublished material may be cited for *provenance and motivation only* — no proof in the standalone paper may depend on an unpublished result. The one spot that needs care is §6, where the sector-tag grounding cites the 2015/2016 manuscripts; I'll keep the full paper's hedge that the sector energies are used as a *definition* and nothing downstream depends on the manuscript results. Your two arXiv preprints cite normally.

Now the conversion — this means pulling the proofs that currently live in the 25pp draft into the condensed paper (lift, dichotomy, both no-gos with the block-decomposition computation, the anomaly lemma and rate theorem, the grading lemma), making the numerics appendix self-contained against the anc/ package, and removing ZS/SI from the bibliography entirely.

Done — the standalone version is delivered above (PDF, tex, and rebuilt tarball), saved to the project, and the status doc updated.

**What changed.** Every proof that used to be delegated to the 25-page draft now lives in the paper: the lift theorem with its proper domain, the two maximality propositions (including the block-decomposition computation, which the degree no-go now reuses), the equivariant dichotomy, both no-gos in full, the grading and diagonal-anomaly lemmas, and the rate criterion with the Y=0 branch. The DH function and the η(w) parametrization are defined in-text, the numerics section is self-contained with the two certification tables and both figures, and the title dropped "overview": *The zero-sphere program for the Riemann Hypothesis and the Second Involution Conjecture*, 19 pages. A second adversarial audit compared every transplanted proof against the source — one real catch (the lift theorem's domain hypothesis had been silently globalized, which would be false for entire F at the ruling at infinity) plus a handful of smaller restorations, all fixed. Citations and bibliography are now exactly bijective at 38 entries, with no reference anywhere to a companion paper.

**On your unpublished material** — my recommendation, now implemented: cite it for provenance and motivation only, through the single Zenodo DOI, and keep it out of the arXiv supplementary files (anc/ stays code and data, which is what referees expect there). Bundling the manuscripts as ancillary would make them look load-bearing; the Zenodo deposit gives you the same discoverability plus a timestamped priority record for the 2015–2026 arc. The audit confirmed no proof in the paper depends logically on anything unpublished — the one place that leans on the 2015/2016 manuscripts (the sector-tag grounding in §6) carries an explicit "motivation only; used as a definition here" disclaimer, and I removed the Q_ℓ symbol from a theorem statement where it would have been an undefined reference. One practical consequence: **the Zenodo deposit is now blocking for submission**, since the conjecture's stated provenance and the §6 grounding both point at that DOI placeholder.

The tarball is upload-ready once you've done your read-through and filled the DOI — swap in your edited tex and re-tar; the figures and anc/ are final unless the numerics change.
